question: The standard reference procedure for conducting medico-legal autopsies in India is codified in:

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The NHRC 1997 guidelines specifically govern custodial death autopsies, not the general ML autopsy procedure.

answers.text: The Government of India's proforma for post-mortem examination (ML-2 / ML-3 forms)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The GoI proforma — using forms ML-2 (inquest report) and ML-3 (PM certificate) — sets out the reference standard for conducting and documenting the medico-legal autopsy in India.
Incorrect. The IMC Act governs medical practice registration; it does not specify autopsy procedure standards.
Incorrect. The WHO guidelines are reference documents; the binding Indian standard is the GoI proforma set.

overallFeedback.feedback: The governing reference for medico-legal autopsy in India is the Government of India's proforma (ML-2/ML-3 forms), not the NHRC guidelines (which are custodial-death specific) or international documents.
Well done. The GoI proforma (ML-2/ML-3) is the binding reference for documentation in Indian medico-legal autopsies.
